original_question: Let g:[l]->[l] be a Costas permutation. Does there always exist a larger Costas permutation f having an arithmetic-progression substructure S1,S2 as in Definition 8 such that g(i) = (f(a1 + b1 i) - a2)/b2 on those progressions, so that g is a sub-permutation of f? Is this always true at least for particular families such as sporadic Costas permutations?
target_in_paper: Section 4.3, Problem 8 (immediately after Definition 8): whether every Costas permutation occurs as a sub-permutation of some Costas permutation, with the paper explicitly asking this also for specific families such as sporadic Costas permutations.

refined_question: Let [n]={1,\dots,n}, and let g:[l]->[l] be a Costas permutation (that is, a bijection whose distance vectors are all distinct). Does there exist a Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] for some n, together with integers a1,a2 and positive integers b1,b2, such that the arithmetic-progression sets S_j={a_j+b_j i : i in [l]} are subsets of [n] for j=1,2, satisfy f(S1)=S2, and obey g(i)=(f(a1+b1 i)-a2)/b2 for every i in [l]? Equivalently, is every Costas permutation a sub-permutation of some Costas permutation in the precise sense of Definition 8? In particular, does this hold for specific families of Costas permutations, such as sporadic Costas permutations?
justification: This draft is targeting Section 4.3, Definition 8 and Problem 8 (page 9), not a broader neighboring problem: it uses the exact arithmetic-progression restriction/rescaling setup of Definition 8 and repeats the paper’s special-family clause about sporadic Costas permutations. To make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the rewrite restores the paper’s base notation [n]={1,...,n} from Section 3 (page 2), the definition of Costas permutation from Definition 1 (Section 3.1, page 2), the meaning of 'sporadic' from Definition 6 (Section 3.2.3, page 5), and all of the quantifiers and hypotheses built into Definition 8 (Section 4.3, page 9). It also removes the extra strengthening 'larger', since Problem 8 itself does not impose that restriction.
